newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr closes sharply weaker, seen testing lower.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr closes sharply weaker, seen testing lower.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar sagged over half a U.S. cent to an 18-month low on Wednesday and despite recovering a touch by the close looked set to plump new depths, dealers said.
"It got a little bit of strength in the afternoon here from a firmer Australian dollar, but it's still basically looking soft," said a bank chief dealer said.
The Kiwi closed at US$0.6593/00 and at 65.55 on its Trade-Weighted Index, down from 0.6627/32 and 65.83 at the open.
It plunged to an 18-month low of 0.6578 at mid-session.

"It's just really been a factor of continued selling interest on any rally. There aren't too many buyers around at the moment and sentiment seems to still be pretty negative towards the currency," said the chief dealer.
"At the moment there just seems to be a general disinvestment out of Australia, New Zealand and South East Asia to be honest."
Dealers there was a general flight to "quality" at present, with the greenback and sterling benefitting at the expense of Asian currencies.
"I think we're going to see a few short-covering rallies... but to me it looks like the Kiwi is ready to head towards the 64.5 to 65 (U.S.) cent area," said one.
The Kiwi was seen trading in a 0.6570-6605 range overnight.
